steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with the gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere. Sunlight contains all colors of visible light, but shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) are scattered much more strongly than longer wavelengths (red and orange). Although violet light is scattered even more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue light and some violet is absorbed in the upper atmosphere, so we perceive the sky as blue.
